findings.change_summary: Re-verified, unchanged, applying the news-recency test (fetch_timeline.py run first; existing timeline already carries a 'shelved'/'inferred 2 y' entry at 2023, tl_order 4 -- no new timeline entry needed since the call is unchanged). Most recent activity is only weeks old: on 2 June 2026 Energy World Corp (ASX:EWC) agreed to sell the two Siemens SGT6-5000F gas turbines and one steam turbine long held idle at Pagbilao to US-listed Hallador Energy for US$350m, booking a ~US$285m non-cash impairment against the power-plant assets (17 years after the project's 2009 launch, having never reached commercial operation). Because this activity is <2 years old, the case falls in the 'stays shelved (blue-confirm)' bucket, not the >=4y 'escalate to inferred cancelled' bucket -- so Status and ShelvedYear are left unchanged and simply re-verified. EWC's own framing (per its ASX filings covered by these sources) is that turbine-sale proceeds will fund 'continued development of the Pagbilao LNG platform ... as a standalone third-party access facility', i.e. the company has NOT declared the import terminal itself cancelled, only decoupled it from the now-abandoned integrated power plant -- consistent with keeping the terminal at 'shelved' rather than escalating to 'cancelled'. IEEFA and local Quezon community/church groups (PMCJ, QUEEN) independently characterize the turbine divestment as confirming the wider project is a stranded asset that never advanced past ~70% construction (as of 2024) with no PPA/gas supply secured, supporting continued 'shelved' (not operating, not moving to construction) rather than any upgrade in status. No new construction, PPA, or FEED news found -- the terminal remains dormant; only the equipment/strategy news is new. This also fills the previously blank Status [ref] and ShelvedYear [ref] cells (Rule F: valid fill targets since both paired values already exist and are unchanged).

qa_notes: ieefa.org and businessmirror.com.ph both 403 bot-block on direct fetch; verified instead via their Wayback Machine snapshots (20260611) per the bot-block-is-not-dead rule -- both PASS with the claimed value present, so used as citations.

climatejustice.ph and stocksdownunder.com/tradingview(smallcaps syndication) also passed verification independently and corroborate the same facts (turbine sale date, impairment, EWC's standalone-terminal framing); not all included as refs to avoid an unwieldy ref list, but available if a 4th corroboration is wanted.
smallcaps.com.au direct article and the Aug 2025 ASX PDF could not be verified (scanned/no extractable text or missing token) -- dropped, not relied on.

No evidence found that the LNG import terminal itself is under active construction, has a signed PPA, or has any binding third-party access agreement; EWC's 'continued development' language is a stated intent, not a confirmed construction milestone -- status is being re-verified as unchanged (shelved), not upgraded.
summary: Status verdict: STAYS SHELVED (blue re-verify, unchanged), not escalated to inferred-cancelled. Most recent activity is Energy World Corp's 2 June 2026 sale of the long-idle Pagbilao turbines to Hallador Energy (US$350m) plus a ~US$285m impairment -- under 2 months old, so the news-recency test keeps this in the '<2y: stays shelved' bucket rather than the '>=4y: escalate to cancelled' bucket. EWC's own stated plan is to keep developing the LNG import terminal as a standalone third-party facility (power plant/turbines abandoned separately), which argues against calling the terminal itself cancelled. Filled the previously blank Status [ref] and ShelvedYear [ref] with 3 independent, verified sources (greentechlead.com, IEEFA via Wayback, BusinessMirror via Wayback) -- green-level corroboration. No timeline edit needed; the existing 2023 shelved/inferred-2y timeline entry stands.
